    How it Works. How does Signal work?
    About this result
    Feedback
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Signal works by providing free, encrypted messaging and calls, using end-to-end encryption (E2EE) to ensure only participants can read messages, not even Signal itself, functioning like other chat apps but prioritizing privacy with features like disappearing messages, username support (hiding phone numbers), and secure calls/video chats for individuals and groups. It links contacts via phone numbers but allows usernames to protect privacy, and messages are secured with keys that change frequently, preventing snooping. 
    This video provides a beginner's tutorial on how to use the Signal app:
    57s
    Kevin Stratvert
    YouTube · Apr 25, 2023
    Core Mechanics
    • End-to-End Encryption (E2EE): Signal's key feature; messages are encrypted on the sender's device and decrypted only on the recipient's, using the Signal Protocol, making them unreadable to servers or third parties. 
    • Phone Number Registration: Users sign up with a phone number to find contacts, but recent features allow hiding it with usernames. 
    • Contact Discovery: The app checks your contacts to see who else uses Signal, allowing you to message them directly. 
    Key Features for Privacy & Security
    • Sealed Sender: Hides message sender information from the server. 
    • Disappearing Messages: Messages can be set to self-destruct after a chosen time. 
    • Safety Number Verification: Allows users to verify the authenticity of contacts to prevent impersonation. 
    • Data Minimization: Signal collects very little user data, focusing on privacy by design. 
    You can watch this video to learn why Signal is considered a secure messaging app:
    54s
    CNET
    YouTube · Mar 30, 2025
    How to Use It (Basic Functions)
    • Send Messages: Tap the pencil icon to start a chat, select a contact, and type. 
    • Make Calls: Tap the phone or video camera icon in a chat for encrypted voice or video calls. 
    • Group Chats: Create groups and manage settings like who can add members. 
    • Share Content: Send photos, files, stickers, GIFs, and locations. 
    This video demonstrates how to use the Signal app for sending messages and calls:
    58s
    Cyber-Seniors
    YouTube · Jun 9, 2023
    Platform Availability
    • Cross-Platform: Available on iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
    • Linked Devices: Can link multiple devices to your account, including desktop clients.

      Features. What are the features of Signal?
      About this result
      Feedback
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      Signal's core features include robust end-to-end encryption for all messages and calls, a privacy-focused model with minimal data collection, open-source code for transparency, disappearing messages, and rich media sharing (photos, files, voice notes) within secure group chats, all while operating as a non-profit without ads or trackers. Key privacy tools also involve view-once media, image blurring, call relay, and registration locks for enhanced security.
       
      Security & Privacy
      • End-to-End Encryption: Uses the Signal Protocol for all communication (messages, calls, media). 
      • Minimal Data Collection: Collects virtually no personal data beyond a phone number for registration.
      • Open Source: Code is publicly available for security audits. 
      • No Ads or Trackers: Non-profit model funded by donations, not advertising. 
      • Registration Lock: Protects your account with a PIN.
      • Screen Security: Prevents chat previews in the app switcher and blocks screenshots. 
      • Call Relay: Hides your IP address during calls. 
      • Safety Numbers: Verify contact identities to ensure secure communication. 
      Messaging Features
      • Rich Media: Send texts, photos, videos, GIFs, stickers, voice messages, and files. 
      • Disappearing Messages: Set messages to automatically delete after a set time. 
      • View-Once Media: Photos/videos disappear after the first view, with screenshot prevention on some platforms.
      • Group Chats: Support large groups for communication. 
      • Note to Self: Send messages to yourself across devices. 
      Calls & Media Editing
      • Voice & Video Calls: Secure calls with no long-distance charges. 
      • Image Editing: In-app tools to draw, add text, or automatically blur faces. 
      Customization & More
      • Themes & Appearance: Customize chat colors and themes. 
      • Archiving: Keep muted chats archived. 
      • Stories: Share ephemeral content (optional).

        AI Overview
        Signal is available for mobile on Android and iOS (iPhone/iPad), and for desktop on Windows, macOS, and Linux, with mobile app availability on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. Desktop versions can be downloaded from the official Signal download page and require linking to a phone for use. 
        Mobile Platforms: 
        • Android: Download from the Google Play Store.
        • iOS (iPhone/iPad): Download from the Apple App Store.
        Desktop Platforms: 
        • Windows: Available for 64-bit Windows 7 and newer.
        • macOS: Available for macOS 10.11 (El Capitan) and newer.
        • Linux: Supports 64-bit Debian-based distributions (like Ubuntu, Mint) via APT, and other distros via Snap or Flatpak.
        How to Get Desktop: 
        1. Install Signal on your phone first.
        2. Download the desktop app from signal.org/download.
        3. Link your phone to the desktop app by following the on-screen instructions.

          Privacy Policy. What is the privacy policy of Signal?
          About this result
          Feedback
          An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
          AI Overview
          Signal's privacy policy centers on minimizing data collection, using strong end-to-end encryption (E2EE) for all messages and calls, meaning only sender and recipient can access content, not Signal or third parties. It stores minimal data, primarily your phone number, registration date, and connection times, while message history stays on your device, not their servers. Key aspects include encryption via the Signal Protocol, metadata minimization, and features like usernames to hide phone numbers, all designed for secure, private global communication. 
          Key Principles of Signal's Privacy Policy
          • End-to-End Encryption (E2EE): All communications (messages, calls, media) are encrypted by default, making them unreadable to Signal, governments, or hackers. 
          • Minimal Data Collection: Signal collects very little personal data, primarily your phone number and account creation info, not message content or call logs.
          • Data Stored on Device: Your message history is kept on your device, not on Signal's servers, though messages are briefly queued for delivery if a device is offline. 
          • Metadata Protection: Uses features like "Sealed Sender" to hide who sent a message, limiting what even Signal sees. 
          • Privacy-by-Design: Built to minimize data exposure from the start, making it hard for anyone, including law enforcement with warrants, to get user data. 
          What Signal Collects (and Doesn't)
          • Collects (Minimal): Phone number, account creation date, last connection time.
          • Doesn't Collect: Message content, contact lists, groups, display names, profile pictures, or call content. 
          Privacy Features & Controls
          • Usernames: Allows users to connect without sharing phone numbers. 
          • Registration Lock PIN: Protects against SIM-swap attacks.
          • Safety Numbers: For verifying contact identities. 
          In essence, Signal's policy is to be a secure communication tool that collects as little information as possible, making user privacy its core service, unlike other apps that monetize user data.

            Developers. Who developed Signal?
            About this result
            Feedback
            An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
            AI Overview
            Signal was developed by cryptographer Moxie Marlinspike, who created its predecessors, and Brian Acton, co-founder of WhatsApp, who established the non-profit Signal Foundation in 2018 to support the app, with Acton providing the initial $50 million donation. Signal Messenger LLC, a subsidiary of the Foundation, handles the app's ongoing development, focusing on privacy-centric communication.
             
            Key figures:
            • Moxie Marlinspike:
              The primary creator, who first developed secure messaging technologies (TextSecure, RedPhone) under Whisper Systems, later sold to Twitter, and then continued development under Open Whisper Systems before the Signal Foundation was formed. 
            • Brian Acton:
              Co-founder of WhatsApp, he left Facebook and, in 2018, co-founded the Signal Foundation with Marlinspike, providing significant initial funding to make Signal a sustainable non-profit. 
            Organizational structure:
            • Signal Foundation:
              A non-profit organization dedicated to secure communication, owned by the foundation. 
            • Signal Messenger LLC:
              A subsidiary of the foundation responsible for building the Signal app and protocol.

              Why do people use Signal instead of texting?
              An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
              AI Overview
              People use Signal instead of standard texting primarily
              for its superior, non-profit-driven privacy, offering mandatory end-to-end encryption for all messages and calls, ensuring only users can read them. It does not collect user metadata or store data on servers, making it ideal for high-security, encrypted communication. 
              Key Reasons to Use Signal Over Texting: 
              • Uncompromised Privacy & Security: Unlike SMS, which is unencrypted, Signal uses advanced open-source encryption for every message and call, preventing third parties, including service providers or authorities, from accessing content.
              • Zero Data Retention: Signal does not store your contact list, profile picture, or chat logs. They cannot sell user data, as they don't have it
